items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: we had the original which I mentioned, and then some dates he would add Billy Butterfield on trumpet and Peanut Hucko on clarinet or tenor

ctx.x: When the wonderful, great piano player, Ralph Sutton, visited my house, he looked at the picture and commented, "Where were your sixguns, Cliff?" and I said "Security wouldn't allow me".

And I need an insertion here. That was the Bicentennial that we were playing -- I left out the word 'bi', which was of course, nationwide -- rather, our nation's great celebration. I noticed that in playing this back, that I had talked into this machine, this fool machine here for 10 or 15 minutes about the Lawson-Haggard band, and upon our recording with a larger group, and I forgot to push all the proper buttons. So it was deleted. However, Bob Haggard and Lawson in doing the arrangements, wanted to enlarge…
And of course we added George Burns, who was working at that time on the Hit Parade. So I hope this might be inserted -- it's of importance to me.
